tickets.title: Sonic runs headless as a one-shot query
tickets.what: Owner 2026-11-22: sonic is its own kind, not a herdr worker. Census (157 sonic jobs): 97.5% had no interaction, 0 hud_ask, 2 messages in, 1 lease use, 1 repair; startup 7 s median. Sonic runs headless (pi print/JSON mode, no herdr tab or pane) with a normal job record under $HUD_HOME/jobs: brief in, report out, progress and nesting under its parent still shown in the panel. No hud_ask, no continuation, no idle grace; a failure is final and the caller re-dispatches. hud_lease stays available. Spec: §2.1 says sonic is a headless query role outside the herdr worker rules (draft the sentences; the main session tells the owner).

acceptance.text: hud_create role sonic (main session or a worker child) settles with a report and opens no herdr tab
The panel shows a running and a settled headless sonic under its parent with progress

comments.author: legacy
comments.text: Verified headless print mode with local pi and a synthetic provider. The rebased change passes the full test suite and fixture checks, including a regression test that a legacy Sonic at its role cap does not queue a headless query.

tickets.title: Sonic thinking can be none; lookups lean low; native tools
tickets.what: Owner 2026-11-22: deepseek-v4-1-flash supports none/low/high/max. Add `none` to sonic's thinking_choices (packages/hud-mcp/roles/sonic.json) for running a given command and reporting its output, copying exact text, listing files; tighten the level purposes so narrow named-file lookups pick low (81% of survey sonics picked high after auto-thinking). sonic.md asks for native read/grep/find tools over bash where the harness has them (38.6 bash vs 0 grep per survey). Spec §2.1.4 level list updated (draft; the main session tells the owner).

acceptance.text: The Decision API can pick none, and a command-runner brief does

tickets.title: Sonic checks for loops at 10 minutes and keeps going in the same session
tickets.what:
Owner 2026-11-22 asked whether the 10-minute headless cap fits and what happens to a long query cut off. Facts: of 25 recent sonic jobs with timings, p50 259 s, p90 497 s, 2 over 600 s (677 s and 1,490 s), both finished with outcome done; a fixed 10-minute kill would have failed them and thrown the work away. Owner's design: at 10 minutes do not kill; check whether the query is going round in circles, and if not let the same pi process keep going (same session, prompt cache kept), and never let it go quiet.

- Checkpoint every 10 minutes (`check_s`, default 600). The check reads the recent pi JSON events: it is looping when the last window repeats the same tool calls with the same arguments, or shows no new tool target and no new hud_progress since the previous checkpoint. Looping: stop, settle failed `looping`. Otherwise: keep running and post a progress line ("still working at 10 min: <last step>") that reaches the caller like any progress, so a long query is never silent; the caller may still close it.
- Separate stall rule: no stdout growth and no hud_progress for `stall_s` (default 180) stops it as `stalled`. Safety cap `max_s` (default 1800) stops it as `timeout`. All three are optional sonic role-file fields, shown in `hud_roster(detail:true)`.
- A stopped query keeps its partial stdout; its digest carries the last progress line. Run pi with a session file in the job dir; `hud_create({role:"sonic", retry_of})` on a stopped query resumes that pi session (pi --session) with a short "continue; you were stopped for <reason>" message instead of a fresh start, so context and cache are reused; if the session cannot be resumed, fall back to a new query whose brief carries the original brief plus the partial result.

acceptance.text: A query that keeps making progress runs past 10 minutes in the same process and posts a checkpoint progress line
A synthetic query repeating the same tool call is stopped at the checkpoint as `looping`; a silent one as `stalled` after stall_s; max_s as `timeout`
retry_of on a stopped sonic resumes its pi session (fallback: partial result in the brief)
role-file values change the limits; npm test and check:fixtures pass
